<a id="body"></a>

## Body

A requested or submitted /model command is not evidence that the running model changed. Conversely, an unchanged settings value does not prove that the switch failed: the user's global default may already equal the requested return model.

PR #215 closed S215-002 at 952f305936f4596366ccf9b322f11be0cfaaf357; output edaa57f62ead65b120ea390bc3edc760cd099381. An observable transition records the return model; fully observable non-transition retains Sonnet; ambiguous already-target defaults record model None, unconfirmed:true and last_confirmed_model. The equal-default regression asserts registry, audit and byte-identical settings. Do not relabel an unconfirmed outcome as actual Sonnet.

For global settings restoration, save original bytes or file absence, not only parsed model values. Refuse unreadable/invalid snapshots before switching. Restore original bytes when only model changed; preserve concurrent other-key changes with exact:false; report restoration errors explicitly. Byte identity, atomic replacement and whole-operation cleanup are different guarantees.

S215-N003 remains the cancellation/shutdown cleanup proof ceiling. S215-N004 remains post-submit read-error classification: a failed observation must not silently become proof of Sonnet. The fixes used source and CI proof, not reviewer access to real user settings or live panes.
